sanskrit: na jānīte hi yaḥ śreyaḥ śreyasaś cāvamanyate sa kṣipraṃ bhraśyate rājyān na ca śreyo 'nuvindati
english: The man who does not know where his good lies, and who scorns it even when it is shown to him, swiftly falls from his kingdom and never attains the good.

sanskrit: praṇipatya hi rājānaṃ rājyaṃ yadi labhemahi śreyaḥ syān na tu mauḍhyena rājan gantuṃ parābhavam
english: If by bowing before the king we might regain the kingdom, that would be the better course, O king; to go down to ruin through sheer folly is not.

sanskrit: vaicitravīryavacanāt kṛpāśīlo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ viniyuñjīta rājye tvāṃ govindavacanena ca
english: At a word from the son of Vicitravīrya, and at a word from Govinda, the compassionate Yudhiṣṭhira would install you in your kingdom.

sanskrit: yad brūyād dhi hṛṣīkeśo rājānam aparājitam arjunaṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca sarvaṃ kuryur asaṃśayam
english: Whatever Hṛṣīkeśa should bid the unvanquished king, and Arjuna, and Bhīmasena—all of it they would do, without a doubt.

sanskrit: nātikramiṣyate kṛṣṇo vacanaṃ kauravasya ha dhṛtarāṣṭrasya manye 'haṃ nāpi kṛṣṇasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa, I think, will not transgress the word of the Kaurava Dhṛtarāṣṭra; nor will the son of Pāṇḍu transgress the word of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: etat kṣamam ahaṃ manye tava pārthair avigraham na tvā bravīmi kārpaṇyān na prāṇaparirakṣaṇāt pathyaṃ rājan bravīmi tvāṃ tat parāsuḥ smariṣyasi
english: I hold a peace with the sons of Pṛthā to be the fitting course for you. I do not speak to you out of weakness, nor to save my own life; I speak to you what is wholesome, O king—and when your breath has fled, you will remember it.

sanskrit: iti vṛddho vilapyaitat kṛpaḥ śāradvato vacaḥ dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya śuśoca ca mumoha ca
english: Having lamented thus, the aged Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, drew a long, hot sigh, and grieved, and swooned away.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktas tato rājā gautamena yaśasvinā niḥśvasya dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca tūṣṇīm āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by the illustrious son of Gautama, the king, O lord of peoples, drew a long, hot sigh and fell silent.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtaṃ sa dhyātvā dhārtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ kṛpaṃ śāradvataṃ vākyam ity uvāca paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then, having pondered a while, the high-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that scorcher of foes, spoke these words to Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cit suhṛdā vācyaṃ tat sarvaṃ śrāvito hy aham kṛtaṃ ca bhavatā sarvaṃ prāṇān saṃtyajya yudhyatā
english: All that a friend should say, I have indeed been made to hear; and all has been done by you, who fought while ready to lay down your very life.

sanskrit: gāhamānam anīkāni yudhyamānaṃ mahārathaiḥ pāṇḍavair atitejobhir lokas tvām anudṛṣṭavān
english: The world has beheld you plunging into the enemy hosts, doing battle with the great chariot-warriors, the Pāṇḍavas of surpassing might.

sanskrit: suhṛdā yad idaṃ vācyaṃ bhavatā śrāvito hy aham na māṃ prīṇāti tat sarvaṃ mumūrṣor iva bheṣajam
english: This counsel, which a friend should give, you have made me hear; yet none of it pleases me, as medicine pleases not a man about to die.

sanskrit: hetukāraṇasaṃyuktaṃ hitaṃ vacanam uttamam ucyamānaṃ mahābāho na me viprāgrya rocate
english: This excellent and salutary speech, furnished with reasons and grounds, though it is spoken, O mighty-armed, foremost of brahmins, finds no favor with me.

sanskrit: rājyād vinikṛto 'smābhiḥ kathaṃ so 'smāsu viśvaset akṣadyūte ca nṛpatir jito 'smābhir mahādhanaḥ sa kathaṃ mama vākyāni śraddadhyād bhūya eva tu
english: Cheated by us of his kingdom, how should that king trust us? At the game of dice that king of great wealth was beaten by us; how, then, should he ever again put faith in my words?

sanskrit: tathā dautyena saṃprāptaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pārthahite rataḥ pralabdhaś ca hṛṣīkeśas tac ca karma virodhitam sa ca me vacanaṃ brahman katham evābhimaṃsyate
english: And Kṛṣṇa, who came as an envoy, intent on the welfare of the sons of Pṛthā—Hṛṣīkeśa too was deceived, and that deed of mine bred enmity; how then, O brahmin, will he ever heed a word of mine?

sanskrit: vilalāpa hi yat kṛṣṇā sabhāmadhye sameyuṣī na tan marṣayate kṛṣṇo na rājyaharaṇaṃ tathā
english: What Kṛṣṇā lamented when she came into the midst of the assembly hall, that Kṛṣṇa does not forgive, nor likewise the seizure of the kingdom.

sanskrit: ekaprāṇāv ubhau kṛṣṇāv anyonyaṃ prati saṃhatau purā yac chrutam evāsīd adya paśyāmi tat prabho
english: The two Kṛṣṇas are bound to each other as a single life, joined together as one; what once I had only heard, that, O lord, I now behold.

sanskrit: svasrīyaṃ ca hataṃ śrutvā duḥkhaṃ svapiti keśavaḥ kṛtāgaso vayaṃ tasya sa madarthaṃ kathaṃ kṣamet
english: Hearing that his sister's son was slain, Keśava sleeps in sorrow; we have done him grievous wrong—how should he forgive it for my sake?

sanskrit: abhimanyor vināśena na śarma labhate 'rjunaḥ sa kathaṃ maddhite yatnaṃ prakariṣyati yācitaḥ
english: Through the destruction of Abhimanyu, Arjuna finds no peace; how, though entreated, should he exert himself for my welfare?

sanskrit: madhyamaḥ pāṇḍavas tīkṣṇo bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ pratijñātaṃ ca tenograṃ sa bhajyeta na saṃnamet
english: The middle son of Pāṇḍu, the fierce Bhīmasena of mighty strength, has sworn a dreadful oath; he would break sooner than he would bend.

sanskrit: ubhau tau baddhanistriṃśāv ubhau cābaddhakaṅkaṭau kṛtavairāv ubhau vīrau yamāv api yamopamau
english: Both have girded on their swords, both have buckled on their mail; both heroes have made themselves my foes—the twins too, who are like unto Yama.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca kṛtavairau mayā saha tau kathaṃ maddhite yatnaṃ prakuryātāṃ dvijottama
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin have both made themselves my enemies; how, O best of the twice-born, should those two exert themselves for my good?

sanskrit: duḥśāsanena yat kṛṣṇā ekavastrā rajasvalā parikliṣṭā sabhāmadhye sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: How Kṛṣṇā, clad in a single garment, in her courses, was tormented by Duḥśāsana in the midst of the assembly, before the eyes of all the people—

sanskrit: tathā vivasanāṃ dīnāṃ smaranty adyāpi pāṇḍavāḥ na nivārayituṃ śakyāḥ saṃgrāmāt te paraṃtapāḥ
english: remembering her thus, half-stripped and wretched, even now the Pāṇḍavas, those scorchers of foes, cannot be turned back from battle.

sanskrit: yadā ca draupadī kṛṣṇā madvināśāya duḥkhitā ugraṃ tepe tapaḥ kṛṣṇā bhartṝṇām arthasiddhaye sthaṇḍile nityadā śete yāvad vairasya yātanā
english: And when Draupadī Kṛṣṇā, grieving, performed fierce austerities for my undoing—Kṛṣṇā, for the fulfillment of her husbands' cause, lies ever upon the bare ground, so long as the requital of the feud endures.

sanskrit: nikṣipya mānaṃ darpaṃ ca vāsudevasahodarā kṛṣṇāyāḥ preṣyavad bhūtvā śuśrūṣāṃ kurute sadā
english: Casting aside pride and arrogance, the sister of Vāsudeva, become as a serving-maid, ever waits in attendance upon Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: iti sarvaṃ samunnaddhaṃ na nirvāti kathaṃ cana abhimanyor vināśena sa saṃdheyaḥ kathaṃ mayā
english: Thus all is inflamed, and in no wise can it be quenched; through the slaying of Abhimanyu, how is peace to be made by me with him?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca nāma bhuktvemāṃ pṛthivīṃ sāgarāmbarām pāṇḍavānāṃ prasādena bhuñjīyāṃ rājyam alpakam
english: And how, having enjoyed this earth girdled by the seas, should I enjoy a petty kingdom by the grace of the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: upary upari rājñāṃ vai jvalito bhāskaro yathā yudhiṣṭhiraṃ kathaṃ paścād anuyāsyāmi dāsavat
english: I who blazed above all kings, one above another, like the radiant sun—how should I now follow behind Yudhiṣṭhira like a slave?

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhuktvā svayaṃ bhogān dattvā dāyāṃś ca puṣkalān kṛpaṇaṃ vartayiṣyāmi kṛpaṇaiḥ saha jīvikām
english: Having myself enjoyed all delights and bestowed lavish gifts, how should I lead a beggarly livelihood in the company of the wretched?

sanskrit: nābhyasūyāmi te vākyam uktaṃ snigdhaṃ hitaṃ tvayā na tu saṃdhim ahaṃ manye prāptakālaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I find no fault with your words, spoken in affection and for my good; yet in no wise do I deem this peace to be timely.

sanskrit: sunītam anupaśyāmi suyuddhena paraṃtapa nāyaṃ klībayituṃ kālaḥ saṃyoddhuṃ kāla eva naḥ
english: By a good fight I foresee good policy, O scorcher of foes; this is no time to play the coward—now is our time for battle.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ me bahubhir yajñair dattā vipreṣu dakṣiṇāḥ prāptāḥ kramaśrutā vedāḥ śatrūṇāṃ mūrdhni ca sthitam
english: I have sacrificed with many sacrifices, bestowed largesse upon brahmins, gained the Vedas heard in due succession, and trodden upon the heads of my foes.

sanskrit: bhṛtyā me subhṛtās tāta dīnaś cābhyuddhṛto janaḥ yātāni pararāṣṭrāṇi svarāṣṭram anupālitam
english: My dependents have been well maintained, dear sir, and the wretched folk uplifted; the realms of enemies have been overrun, and my own realm protected.

sanskrit: bhuktāś ca vividhā bhogās trivargaḥ sevito mayā pitṝṇāṃ gatam ānṛṇyaṃ kṣatradharmasya cobhayoḥ
english: Manifold pleasures have been enjoyed, and the threefold aim of life pursued by me; the debt to the ancestors is discharged, and likewise the duty of the warrior—both.

sanskrit: na dhruvaṃ sukham astīha kuto rājyaṃ kuto yaśaḥ iha kīrtir vidhātavyā sā ca yuddhena nānyathā
english: No happiness is lasting here below—whence then a kingdom, whence renown? Fame is to be won in this world, and that by battle and no otherwise.

sanskrit: gṛhe yat kṣatriyasyāpi nidhanaṃ tad vigarhitam adharmaḥ sumahān eṣa yac chayyāmaraṇaṃ gṛhe
english: Even for a warrior, death within his house is a thing condemned; a most grievous unrighteousness is this—to die in bed at home.

sanskrit: araṇye yo vimuñceta saṃgrāme vā tanuṃ naraḥ kratūn āhṛtya mahato mahimānaṃ sa gacchati
english: The man who lays down his body in the wilderness or in battle, having offered great sacrifices, attains to glory.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇaṃ vilapann ārto jarayābhipariplutaḥ mriyate rudatāṃ madhye jñātīnāṃ na sa pūruṣaḥ
english: He who, wailing piteously and afflicted, overwhelmed by old age, dies amid weeping kinsmen—that man is no man at all.

sanskrit: tyaktvā tu vividhān bhogān prāptānāṃ paramāṃ gatim apīdānīṃ suyuddhena gaccheyaṃ satsalokatām
english: Having forsaken manifold delights, may I even now, by a good fight, attain that supreme goal which they have reached—the realm of the righteous.

sanskrit: śūrāṇām āryavṛttānāṃ saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinām dhīmatāṃ satyasaṃdhānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kratuyājinām
english: For heroes of noble conduct, who never turn back in battle, wise men true to their word, all of them performers of sacrifice—

sanskrit: śastrāvabhṛtham āptānāṃ dhruvaṃ vāsas triviṣṭape mudā nūnaṃ prapaśyanti śubhrā hy apsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: for those who have attained the final ablution of weapons, a sure dwelling is in heaven; surely the radiant troops of apsarases behold them with joy.

sanskrit: paśyanti nūnaṃ pitaraḥ pūjitāñ śakrasaṃsadi apsarobhiḥ parivṛtān modamānāṃs triviṣṭape
english: Surely the ancestors behold them honored in the assembly of Śakra, encircled by apsarases, rejoicing in heaven.

sanskrit: panthānam amarair yātaṃ śūraiś caivānivartibhiḥ api taiḥ saṃgataṃ mārgaṃ vayam apy āruhemahi
english: The path trodden by the immortals and by heroes who never turn back—that road which they have joined, may we too ascend.

sanskrit: pitāmahena vṛddhena tathācāryeṇa dhīmatā jayadrathena karṇena tathā duḥśāsanena ca
english: By the aged grandsire, and by the wise preceptor, by Jayadratha and by Karṇa, and likewise by Duḥśāsana—

sanskrit: ghaṭamānā madarthe 'smin hatāḥ śūrā janādhipāḥ śerate lohitāktāṅgāḥ pṛthivyāṃ śaravikṣatāḥ
english: those heroes, those lords of men, striving in this cause of mine, lie slain, their limbs smeared with blood, mangled by arrows upon the earth.

sanskrit: uttamāstravidaḥ śūrā yathoktakratuyājinaḥ tyaktvā prāṇān yathānyāyam indrasadmasu dhiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Those heroes, masters of the highest weapons, who sacrificed with rites as enjoined, having laid down their lives according to the law, are stationed in the halls of Indra.

sanskrit: tais tv ayaṃ racitaḥ panthā durgamo hi punar bhavet saṃpatadbhir mahāvegair ito yādbhiś ca sadgatim
english: By them has this path been laid out—a path that would be hard to tread again—by those who fell with mighty speed and went hence to the goal of the good.

sanskrit: ye madarthe hatāḥ śūrās teṣāṃ kṛtam anusmaran ṛṇaṃ tat pratimuñcāno na rājye mana ādadhe
english: Remembering the deeds of those heroes who were slain in my cause, and seeking to discharge that debt to them, I set not my mind upon the kingdom.

sanskrit: pātayitvā vayasyāṃś ca bhrātṝn atha pitāmahān jīvitaṃ yadi rakṣeyaṃ loko māṃ garhayed dhruvam
english: Having brought down my comrades, my brothers, and my grandsires, were I to guard my own life, the world would surely revile me.

sanskrit: kīdṛśaṃ ca bhaved rājyaṃ mama hīnasya bandhubhiḥ sakhibhiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca praṇipatya ca pāṇḍavam
english: And what manner of kingdom would it be for me, bereft of kinsmen, of companions and of friends, and won by bowing before the son of Pāṇḍu?

sanskrit: so 'ham etādṛśaṃ kṛtvā jagato 'sya parābhavam suyuddhena tataḥ svargaṃ prāpsyāmi na tad anyathā
english: I, then, having wrought such ruin upon this world, shall thereafter by a good fight attain to heaven, and not otherwise.

sanskrit: evaṃ duryodhanenoktaṃ sarve saṃpūjya tad vacaḥ sādhu sādhv iti rājānaṃ kṣatriyāḥ saṃbabhāṣire
english: When Duryodhana had spoken thus, all the warriors honored that speech and addressed the king, crying, "Well said, well said!"

sanskrit: parājayam aśocantaḥ kṛtacittāś ca vikrame sarve suniścitā yoddhum udagramanaso 'bhavan
english: Grieving not over their defeat, and resolved upon valor, all were firmly determined to fight, and grew exalted in spirit.

sanskrit: tato vāhān samāśvāsya sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ ūne dviyojane gatvā pratyatiṣṭhanta kauravāḥ
english: Then, having refreshed their mounts, all the Kauravas, rejoicing in the prospect of battle, having gone a little less than two yojanas, halted and took their stand.

sanskrit: ākāśe vidrume puṇye prasthe himavataḥ śubhe aruṇāṃ sarasvatīṃ prāpya papuḥ sasnuś ca tajjalam
english: On a clear and holy, coral-hued tableland of Himavat, fair to behold, reaching the red Sarasvatī, they drank and bathed in its waters.

sanskrit: tava putrāḥ kṛtotsāhāḥ paryavartanta te tataḥ paryavasthāpya cātmānam anyonyena punas tadā sarve rājan nyavartanta kṣatriyāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Your sons, their resolve renewed, then turned about; and steadying themselves once more, the one through the other, all the warriors, O king, urged on by fate, returned again.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atha haimavate prasthe sthitvā yuddhābhinandinaḥ sarva eva mahārāja yodhās tatra samāgatāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Now, halting upon that tableland of Himavat, all the warriors, rejoicing in battle, O great king, gathered together there.

sanskrit: śalyaś ca citrasenaś ca śakuniś ca mahārathaḥ aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: Śalya and Citrasena, and Śakuni the great chariot-warrior, Aśvatthāman too, and Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas—

sanskrit: suṣeṇo 'riṣṭasenaś ca dhṛtasenaś ca vīryavān jayatsenaś ca rājānas te rātrim uṣitās tataḥ
english: Suṣeṇa and Ariṣṭasena, and the valiant Dhṛtasena, and king Jayatsena—these spent the night there.

sanskrit: raṇe karṇe hate vīre trāsitā jitakāśibhiḥ nālabhañ śarma te putrā himavantam ṛte girim
english: When the hero Karṇa had been slain in battle, terrified by the foes who bore the marks of victory, your sons found no refuge save the mountain Himavat.

sanskrit: te 'bruvan sahitās tatra rājānaṃ sainyasaṃnidhau kṛtayatnā raṇe rājan saṃpūjya vidhivat tadā
english: Gathered together there, they spoke to the king before the army; having striven in battle, O king, and having honored him then with due ceremony, they said:

sanskrit: kṛtvā senāpraṇetāraṃ parāṃs tvaṃ yoddhum arhasi yenābhiguptāḥ saṃgrāme jayemāsuhṛdo vayam
english: "Having appointed a leader of the host, you should do battle with the foe, under whose protection in the fray we may conquer our enemies."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ sthitvā rathe rathavarottamam sarvayuddhavibhāgajñam antakapratimaṃ yudhi
english: Then Duryodhana, standing upon his chariot, looked upon that foremost of chariot-warriors, versed in every division of warfare, the very likeness of Death in battle—

sanskrit: svaṅgaṃ pracchannaśirasaṃ kambugrīvaṃ priyaṃvadam vyākośapadmābhimukhaṃ vyāghrāsyaṃ merugauravam
english: fair of limb, his head well-covered, his neck shapely as a conch, gracious in speech, his face like an opened lotus, tiger-mouthed, weighty as Meru—

sanskrit: sthāṇor vṛṣasya sadṛśaṃ skandhanetragatisvaraiḥ puṣṭaśliṣṭāyatabhujaṃ suvistīrṇaghanorasam
english: in shoulders, eyes, gait, and voice like the bull of the Steadfast One, his arms full, firm, and long, his chest broad and massive—

sanskrit: jave bale ca sadṛśam aruṇānujavātayoḥ ādityasya tviṣā tulyaṃ buddhyā cośanasā samam
english: in speed and in strength like the younger brother of Aruṇa and like the Wind, in radiance equal to the Sun, and in wisdom the peer of Uśanas—

sanskrit: kāntirūpamukhaiśvaryais tribhiś candramasopamam kāñcanopalasaṃghātaiḥ sadṛśaṃ śliṣṭasaṃdhikam
english: in loveliness, beauty, and the majesty of his countenance—these three—comparable to the moon, like a mass of golden stone, his joints well-knit—

sanskrit: suvṛttorukaṭījaṅghaṃ supādaṃ svaṅgulīnakham smṛtvā smṛtvaiva ca guṇān dhātrā yatnād vinirmitam
english: with shapely thighs, hips, and legs, fair feet, and comely fingers and nails, fashioned with care by the Creator, who called to mind virtue upon virtue—

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ nipuṇaṃ śrutisāgaram jetāraṃ tarasārīṇām ajeyaṃ śatrubhir balāt
english: endowed with every auspicious mark, skilled, an ocean of sacred lore, a conqueror of foes by his swiftness, himself unconquerable by enemies through force—

sanskrit: daśāṅgaṃ yaś catuṣpādam iṣvastraṃ veda tattvataḥ sāṅgāṃś ca caturo vedān samyag ākhyānapañcamān
english: him who knows in truth the science of archery with its ten branches and four feet, and the four Vedas with their auxiliaries, with the sacred narratives as a fifth—

sanskrit: ārādhya tryambakaṃ yatnād vratair ugrair mahātapāḥ ayonijāyām utpanno droṇenāyonijena yaḥ
english: the great ascetic who, having earnestly propitiated the Three-Eyed One with fierce vows, was begotten by Droṇa, himself not born of a womb, upon a woman not born of a womb—

sanskrit: tam apratimakarmāṇaṃ rūpeṇāsadṛśaṃ bhuvi pāragaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ guṇārṇavam aninditam tam abhyetyātmajas tubhyam aśvatthāmānam abravīt
english: him of matchless deeds, in beauty unequaled upon earth, master of all the sciences, an ocean of virtues, the blameless one—approaching that Aśvatthāman, O king, your son spoke to him:

sanskrit: yaṃ puraskṛtya sahitā yudhi jeṣyāma pāṇḍavān guruputro 'dya sarveṣām asmākaṃ paramā gatiḥ bhavāṃs tasmān niyogāt te ko 'stu senāpatir mama
english: "With whom set at our head, united, we may vanquish the Pāṇḍavas in battle—the preceptor's son this day is the supreme refuge of us all. By your appointment, then, who shall be commander of my host?"

sanskrit: drauṇir uvāca ayaṃ kulena vīryeṇa tejasā yaśasā śriyā sarvair guṇaiḥ samuditaḥ śalyo no 'stu camūpatiḥ
english: The son of Droṇa said: "This Śalya, endowed in birth, in valor, in energy, in renown, in splendor, in every virtue—let him be the leader of our army."

sanskrit: bhāgineyān nijāṃs tyaktvā kṛtajño 'smān upāgataḥ mahāseno mahābāhur mahāsena ivāparaḥ
english: "Forsaking his own sisters' sons, in gratitude he came over to us—lord of a great army, mighty-armed, like a second Mahāsena."

sanskrit: enaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā nṛpatiṃ nṛpasattama śakyaḥ prāptuṃ jayo 'smābhir devaiḥ skandam ivājitam
english: "Having made this king commander of the host, O best of kings, victory may be won by us, as the gods won it through the unconquered Skanda."

sanskrit: tathokte droṇaputreṇa sarva eva narādhipāḥ parivārya sthitāḥ śalyaṃ jayaśabdāṃś ca cakrire yuddhāya ca matiṃ cakrūr āveśaṃ ca paraṃ yayuḥ
english: When the son of Droṇa had spoken thus, all the lords of men stood encircling Śalya and raised shouts of victory; they set their minds upon battle and passed into the highest fervor.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ śalyaṃ bhūmau sthitvā rathe sthitam uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā rāmabhīṣmasamaṃ raṇe
english: Then Duryodhana, standing upon the ground, with joined palms addressed Śalya, who stood upon his chariot, the equal in battle of Rāma and of Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto mitrāṇāṃ mitravatsala yatra mitram amitraṃ vā parīkṣante budhā janāḥ
english: "This is that hour come round, O lover of friends, the hour of friends, wherein wise men put to the test whether one be a friend or no friend."
